Name: Jesus Made
Report: Made vs. Leo is the new Griffin vs. McGonigle which was the new Chourio vs. Holliday which was the new Gunnar vs. Carroll which was the new Witt vs. Julio which was the new Wander vs. Kelenic which was the new Acuna vs. Vlad which was the new ... you get the point. We have an old fashioned #1 prospect standoff right now. Both are 19 years old with excellent across the board production at Double-A. Neither are showing major hit tool issues or groundball issues. Both are running. It's dead even, but someone has to be #1 and it's Made. The tie breaker was the better K% and more steals/better success rate.

Name: Leo De Vries
Report: No shame in being #2 to Made. This is a battle that could flip flop their entire careers.

Name: Edward Florentino
Report: Florentino got a late start to the season but has looked like a superstar since returning, slashing .306/.469/.722 with 4 homers, 1 steal, and a 20.4/24.5 K%/BB% in 11 games split between Single-A and High-A. Maybe it's a little risky moving him to 3rd overall above some of these upper minor bats, but he's showing a level of potential superstar that I'm not sure those upper minors bats are showing at the moment.

Name: Josue De Paula
Report: ... other than De Paula, who most certainly has that superstar potential, but I still fear he's not a guy going to sell out for game power. That is only a quibble though, as he's conquering Double-A with no issue, slashing .309/.442/.454 with 3 homers, 9 steals, and a 15.0/18.3 K%/BB% in 26 games. The 17% whiff% is impressive. Even without selling out for game power, he has the raw juice to hit dingers anyway. The other snafu is the Dodgers. It's really hard to trust this team to actually roll out the red carpet for their young prospects, especially one who isn't great on defense. But other than that, you know Josue has been my guy since he was a complete unknown in the DSL, and with him dominating the upper minors, the restrictor plates are completely off. I was debating Florentino vs. De Paula for awhile, but Florentino's lift/pull and a clear path in Pitt in general is what swayed me.

Name: Walker Jenkins
Report: Down goes Walker again. This time with a shoulder injury after colliding with the OF wall. The Twins curse strikes again ... and again and again and again. So disheartening. He was just starting to heat up at Triple-A and the underlying numbers looked good with a 92.1 MPH EV, 17.8% whiff% and 13.8 degree launch. He would have ranked 3rd, but with yet another injury, I just can't put him there. So frustrating, and maybe this is even still too high but I don't want to kill him yet. If you are fed up, I get it

Name: AJ Ewing
Report: Ewing is my best call on the Predicting the 2027 Top 50 Prospects Rankings this off-season, predicting he would be a Top 10 prospect by this off-season, and writing, "I dropped Corbin Carroll and Pete Crow Armstrong’s name when I called Ewing a major target in 2024 FYPD’s, and now we will see the Carroll/PCA like blow up. The massively underrated power will show up with 14 homers in 120 games in the upper minors. Combined with the speed, plate skills, and defense, everyone will realize this is an elite prospect in both fantasy and real life." ... and now I think he's there already. He has a 92.4 MPH EV with a 50% Hard Hit% in 6 games at Triple-A. His 2 homers has already almost matched his entire homer total from 2025 (3 homers). And of course, everything else is there, slashing .388/.500/.588 with 2 homers, 16 steals, and a 16.0/18.9 K%/BB% in 24 games. He's still not a home run hitter, but this is a fantasy beast even if he can get to 15-20, and there is clearly raw power to tap into down the line. I was all in on Ewing in his draft year, I was all in this off-season, and I'm staying all in. I know this looks high, but using Max Clark as an anchor, why does Clark deserve to be over Ewing? It's close of course, but I think Ewing has the edge

Name: Franklin Arias
Report: I had Arias ranked 46th overall on my End of Season Prospects Rankings. I gave him a strong blurb in my Top 1,000, writing, "The hype has definitely cooled a bit from last off-season, and the funny thing is I now see I might be slightly higher on him than other places, or at least I'm fully on board with his current value."� … and then I just slowly got cold feet and slipped him to 89th overall this off-season. To be fair, 89th overall was about his value other places too, but I just can't help myself with hit tool first types hah … I’m going to keep ranking these types high in the future though, and Arias is proving he deserved a lofty ranking, slashing .359/.433/.731 with 8 homers, 2 steals, and a 11.1/7.8 K%/BB% in 22 games. He’s lifting a lot more with a big leg kick, the raw power should only keep ticking up as he gets older, and he’s now proving the hit/plate skills against advanced competition. I’m still not sure the power/speed combo will be huge, but this is obviously a special bat, and I'm done underrating hit tool first types.

Name: Max Clark
Report: Doing everything at Triple-A but showing power with only 1 homer and a mediocre 35.4% Hard Hit% in 29 games. He's still young and the power is only going to tick up from here, but he's a bit more contact/speed than optimal, and I think it means a few guys sneak past him right now

Name: Colt Emerson
Report: He's only 20 at Triple-A, so we have to grade on a curve, but he hasn't been that great with a 94 wRC+, 29.3% K%, 87.1 MPH EV and 50.8% GB%. Again, he's only 20, and his value holds steady, but he's not blowing up yet

Name: Rainiel Rodriguez
Report: Obliterating High-A like he's obliterated every level before it, slashing .306/.433/.529 with 3 homers, 2 steals, and a 18.3/16.3 K%/BB% in 23 games. There is little doubt this is one of the most special bats in the lower minors. I predicted I was going to be too low on Rodriguez in my Predicting the 2027 Prospects Rankings, ranking him 6th overall (so why didn’t you raise him you ask, idk, I’m stubborn I guess ha)

Name: Seth Hernandez
Report: I have zero regrets about having some caution on high school righties, but he ain't in high school anymore with a 1.23 ERA and 50.0/7.3 K%/BB% in 22 IP. The fastball sits 97.2 MPH and the 3 secondaries (changeup, slider curve) all have about 70% whiff percentages. If you want to find a quibble, the fastball actually isn't missing a ton of bats with a 26.6% whiff%, but that isn't even that bad. His upside seems to be on a level all to himself. He's the new #1 pitching prospect in baseball

Name: Thomas White
Report: 2.13 ERA with a 39.6/8.3 K%/BB% in 12.2 IP at Triple-A. The 95.1 MPH fastball/sweeper combo has been dominant. The change has been solid. He's done nothing to lose his hold on the #1 non debuted prospect in baseball, but Seth Hernandez just took it from him

Name: Kade Anderson
Report: 0.37 ERA with a 43.2/4.5 K%/BB% in 24.1 IP. He still doesn't have the overpowering fastball, so the true test will be vs. MLB hitters, but clearly he is putting the Anderson vs. Doyle to rest, and he's now in the running for #1 pitching prospect in baseball. I just think Hernandez' and White's stuff are on another level, but he's right there

Name: George Lombard
Report: Very clearly looks like the Yanks SS of the future, and that future can come in the 2nd half with across the board destruction of Double-A. He projects as an impact all category contributor. Just when the entire industry cooled on him, the explosion came

Name: Zyhir Hope
Report: Seeing the hit tool transfer was the most important thing in the upper minors, and it's passing with flying colors with a 22.8% K% and 24.1% whiff%. Obviously the majors is the ultimate test, but this is big to see, because the power/speed combo will do the rest (5 homers and 4 steals in 26 games)

Name: Caleb Bonemer
Report: Power is exploding at High-A with 11 homers in 26 games, but the reason I was slightly cautious on Bonemer this off-season was because I thought there could be some hit tool risk against more advanced competition, and that hit tool risk is showing with a 30.3% K% and 34% whiff%. For the record, Bonemer was an FYPD Target for me and I was all over his 2025 breakout. I also love to see him smashing High-A. But I do think we can't completely hand wave away the hit tool risk.

Name: Aidan Miller
Report: Yet to debut with a back injury. Back injuries can be recurring and a constant problem, so it's not a great, but I don't want to completely tank him for it. If I owned him, I would want to remain patient

Name: Sebastian Walcott
Report: Yet to debut with internal brace surgery which he's hoping to return from in August in a best case scenario. We've seen hitters return from TJ/elbow injuries with no problem, so it's really mostly a concern defensively. I'm buying low here.

Name: Robby Snelling
Report: Just patiently waiting for the call to the majors as he beats up on Triple-A hitters

Name: Charlie Condon
Report: Hit tool concerns are stabilizing at Triple-A with a 18.5% K%, although he's only been solid overall with a 107 wRC+. I still want to bet on this power bat in Coors, and he's knocking on the door of the bigs

Name: Braden Montgomery
Report: Just got the call to Triple-A after destroying Double-A (162 wRC+ in 27 games). The GB% is way down too, which is big to see. There is plenty of room for him on the MLB roster. Chicago has been rightfully dogged on for a while, but their time is most certainly coming.

Name: Ralphy Velazquez
Report: Ralphy is one of the more underrated bats in the minors with a 15.0/15.0 K%/BB%, 4 homers, and a 136 wRC+ in 24 games at Double-A as a 20 year old. This is a special power bat

Name: Luis Pena
Report: In a scary moment a couple weeks ago, Pena passed out in the dugout and was rushed to the hospital. Thankfully, he seems to be okay now. There is no timetable for his return, and whenever something like this happens, it feels weird to evaluate their dynasty value. He was bouncing back at High-A after struggling there in 2025, so his value was on the rise before the scare.

Name: Emmanuel Rodriguez
Report: 93.4 MPH EV with a 36.4% whiff% and 21.3% BB% says it all. There is hit tool risk, but the OBP and power should be beastly enough to make him both an impact real life and fantasy bat

Name: Ryan Waldschmidt
Report: Waldschmidt is a really good proximity bat, but if I was going to nitpick, there is some hit tool risk, he doesn't hit the ball overly hard with a 34.9% Hard Hit% and he's only been an okay base stealer in his career. So I guess that is my way of saying don't overrate him too much, even though I still like him a lot.

Name: Emil Morales
Report: My boy Emil is back to destroying Single-A with a 138 wRC+ which he already did last year. Seeing how the hit tool holds up at High-A will be a big test for him, but you already know I'm all in, and I'm staying all in

Name: Josue Briceno
Report: Underwent wrist surgery in spring which is not a great injury for hitters because it's known to linger. There is also no timetable for his return. This probably doesn't change his long term outlook too much though, and short term he was blocked anyway, so I'm not going to ding him too much for it

Name: Justin Gonzales
Report: Zero surprise that the homer power is coming with 4 homers in 22 games. And the contact isn't going anywhere either with a 16.5% K%. He was one of my top targets this off-season, and I want to keep betting big on him. One of the true top hit/power beasts in the minors

Name: Eli Willits
Report: Living up to the hype of the #1 overall pick, slashing .275/.419/.451 with 3 homers, 21 steals, and a 21.7/20.2 K%/BB% in 26 games at Single-A. Keep in mind he is a true 18 year old. He's hitting homers, he's super aggressive on the bases, and he's far advanced for his years.

Name: Luis Hernandez
Report: Dude has 3 homers with a 10.5/10.5 K%/BB% in 4 games in stateside rookie ball after skipping over the DSL completely. This looks like a truly special rocket ship. I'm not even sure this is high enough.

Name: Luis Lara
Report: Lara was once a guy scrapping my Top 100 a few years ago, and now we're full circle with the power breakout here. He has a 43.4% Hard Hit% with 6 homers, a 13.6% whiff% and 12 steals in 33 games at Triple-A. I still don't think he's going to be a huge homer guy in the majors with a 51% GB%, but the power uptick makes him one of the better contact/speed guys in the minors. Frelick and Mitchell aren't going to give up their jobs easily, but they can also be passed, so there is some semblance of a path. And we know how great of a developmental org Milwaukee is.

Name: Pedro Ramirez
Report: 8.6 degree launch with a 43.3% Hard Hit% says maybe have some caution on fully buying into the power explosion. The power is certainly up though, he gets the bat on the ball and he runs, so it's a fun breakout, but maybe the power isn't going to look as big in the majors. And he's also blocked. I'm buying, but those are the reasons I'm not going even higher

Name: Kaelen Culpepper
Report: Power is way up with a 91.4 MPH EV and 49.4% Hard Hit%. He's also lifting it more with a 39.8% GB%. The 100 wRC+ is only okay, but I think that is mostly bad luck. Culpepper was a target for me in his FYPD year, I was all over his 2025 breakout, and I'm loving what I'm seeing in 2026. I'm going to stay high. He's still underrated

Name: Joshua Baez
Report: 33.3% K% and 36.1% whiff% is a bit worrisome with his history of hit tool risk. The elite power/speed combo is shining too though with 7 homers, 6 steals, and a 53.6% Hard Hit%, so he's settling into a very high risk, high reward range rather than building on those 2025 hit tool gains.

Name: Mike Sirota
Report: LA is too stacked for their own good at Double-A with De Paula, Hope and George, so Sirota is stuck decimating High-A again (192 wRC+ in 24 games). Seeing it in the upper minors is the last step towards an explosion, but we are going to have to wait

Name: Eric Hartman
Report: Hartman gives me shades of Jared Kelenic (when he was good in the minors), and he's performing like him in the minors too, slashing .310/.389/.630 with 8 homers, 11 steals, and a 23.9/9.7 K%/BB% in 25 games at High-A. He's still 19, and he's doing it at High-A. The 22% whiff% and 27.8% GB% is excellent. He's looking like a true stud

Name: Josuar Gonzalez
Report: Just returned from a hamstring injury and is starting in rookie ball. I can't imagine it will be long before he gets the call to full season ball if it's hitting

Name: Theo Gillen
Report: Power is exploding with 6 homers in 19 games at High-A, although the 56.8% GB% is quite high, so a bigger sample is needed to see how real it is. I've been high on Gillen since he was drafted, and obviously this is a great start

Name: Braylon Payne
Report: The 32% whiff% is still sticking in my craw a tad, but other than that, he's destroying High=A, slashing .290/.402/.609 with 6 homers, 7 steals, and a 24.4/14.6 K%/BB% in 19 games. He's lifting more, the hit tool is taking a step forward, and keep in mind he's still just 19 years old.

Name: Ethan Holliday
Report: I split the difference between panic and patience after Holliday's rough pro debut, and that turned out to be the right move as he's off to a strong start, slashing .261/.418/.493 with 4 homers, 1 steal, and a 25.3/18.7 K%/BB% in 20 games at High-A. We can heavily dial down the power meter. He looks like a good one

Name: Tyler Bremner
Report: 1.08 ERA with a 39.7/7.9 K%/BB% in 16.2 IP at High-A. Other top college starters went straight to Double-A, but he's dominating the competition put in front of him

Name: Anthony Eyanson
Report: Once we saw the fastball tick up into the mid 90's the breakout was inevitable, and now it's here with a 0.44 ERA and 47.9/4.2 K%/BB% in 20.1 IP at High-A. This guy ripped up the SEC with high K rates even with low 90's heat, so the fastball ticking up is a big deal. Only thing stopping him from an even higher ranking is seeing it in the upper minors.

Name: Eduardo Quintero
Report: Struggling at High-A with a 69 wRC+ but he's been heating up and he's already hit well at the level last year. I think it's just a slow start. I would hold steady on his value

Name: JoJo Parker
Report: Cooled off since his hot start and is now hitting .200 with a 56.9% GB% and 108 wRC+. Some of that BA is clearly bad luck, but his value is more holding steady right now than exploding

Name: Ronny Cruz
Report: Cruz gives me shades of Alfonso Soriano, and he's performing like him too, slashing .343/.436/.616 with 6 homers, 18 steals, and a 22.9/11.9 K%/BB% in 25 games split between Single--A and High-A. The 38.2% whiff% is on the concerning side, but considering the strong K rate, I don't want to overly panic on that.

Name: Tate Southisene
Report: The small sample pro debut steered us wrong in this case. He's slashing .271/.441/.479 with 4 homers, 20 steals, and a 24.4/17.3 K%/BB% in 26 games. Atlanta surprised everyone when they took him 22nd overall, and they are being proved right

Name: Alfredo Duno
Report: Mediocre at High-A with a 96 wRC+, but the 25.7% whiff% and lift/pull look good, so it's only a matter of time before he goes on a homer binge. Hold strong

Name: Ethan Salas
Report: Bouncing back after 2 down seasons as a still 19 year old at Double-A, slashing .307/.402/.573 with 5 homers, 6 steals, and a 24.1/13.8 K%/BB% in 22 games at Double-A. The back looks healthy, the glove makes him a lock to stick behind the plate, and he's back on track to be an impact fantasy catcher

Name: Ryan Sloan
Report: 7.13 ERA with a 24.7/11.1 K%/BB% in 17.2 IP. Upper minors hitters are giving him fits. He's only 20 and the stuff is stuff excellent, so let's give him some time to get comfortable, but this obviously isn't the slicing through the minors outcome I was hoping for

Name: Nathan Flewelling
Report: In the next wave of elite catcher prospect, slashing .321/.407/.641 with 7 homers and a 24.2/12.1 K%/BB% in 22 games at High-A as a 19 year old. There is some hit tool risk with a 28.2% whiff%, but the raw power is huge and now the GB% is way down

Name: Taitn Gray
Report: Has the look of a middle of the order masher, slashing .304/.437/.481 with 3 homers, 3 steals, and a 15.5/19.4 K%/BB% in 23 games. He's still just 18 years old and he's a 6'4'' beast.

Name: Josh Hammond
Report: Slashing .298/.396/.489 with 2 homers, 5 steals, and a 21.6/14.4 K%/BB% in 25 games at Single-A. He's the 28th overall pick, got great backfield reviews, and is now ripping up Single-A

Name: Josiah Hartshorn
Report: He's cooling off since his hot start, but the 14.8/20.9 K%/BB%, 16.1% whiff%, and power at 6'0'', 220 pounds is still a very exciting combination.

Name: Cooper Flemming
Report: Here is what I wrote in the last Rundown about Cooper Flemming, "Flemming has been quietly destroying Single-A. He went 3 for 3 with 2 doubles yesterday and is now slashing .361/.443/.578 with 3 homers, 5 steals, and a 14.4/11.3 K%/BB% in 21 games. This is projectable 6'3'' kid with a sweet as hell lefty swing. The hit tool is clearly transferring with a 16.5% whiff% and he's showing his athleticism too with 5 steals. The only quibble is a 55.1% GB%, but he's still knocking homers out. The hype has really started to boil over on a lot of these 19 year olds blowing up in the lower minors, but it's still relatively quiet on Flemming. If you missed out on the first wave, jump on him now."

Name: Jhonny Level
Report: I called him Michael Arroyo 2.0 this off-season, and he continues to follow that path with him conquering Single-A with across the board destruction

Name: Elian Pena
Report: 22.4% Hard Hit% is the only thing I don't like. Plate skills, base stealing, lift/pull, and production are all there, and he's only 18, so I love the start. But that Hard Hit is very low

Name: Juneiker Caceres
Report: I liked Caceres this off-season, gave him a strong blurb, but then got a little lukewarm with his ranking. But I'm done being lukewarm on hit tool first types, and Caceres is one of the best hit tool first types as an 18 year old in full season ball with a 9.8/15.7 K%/BB%, 2 homers, 4 steals, and a 114 wRC+ in 21 games. The power/speed combo isn't going to be huge, but the hit tool will make up for it

Name: Kendry Chourio
Report: The K/BB King is back to work at Single-A with a 1.65 ERA and 30.6/3.2 K%/BB% in 16.1 IP

Name: Ethan Conrad
Report: Yet to debut with a back injury

Name: Dax Kilby
Report: Yet to debut with a hamstring injury

Name: Jarlin Susana
Report: Yet to debut after undergoing lat surgery in September and there still isn't a timetable on his return

Name: Cam Caminiti
Report: Not dominating High-A, but pitching well with a 3.52 xFIP (4.66 ERA) and a 26.2/7.4 K%/BB% in 29 IP

Name: Spencer Jones
Report: We are seeing Murakami thrive with a 43.6% whiff% (so far), so why not Jones too. Jones also has a 43.5% whiff%, and like Murakami, he smokes the ball with a 95.3 MPH EV. It's the highest risk, highest reward profile in the minors. I want to stay in on this at a reasonable ranking

Name: Lazaro Montes
Report: 7 homers with a 36.8% whiff% and 150 wRC+ in 26 games at Double-A. We've known who Montes was since before he even stepped into pro ball. Low BA, high OBP slugger

Name: Ryan Clifford
Report: We know he's a low BA, high OBP slugger but the 39.8% K% in 31 games at AAA is a bit out of control right now

Name: Xavier Neyens
Report: The power was not oversold with 5 homers and a 153 wRC+ in 20 games at Single-A, but the strikeouts are a bit worse than optimal with a 36.3% K%. The 32.4% whiff% actually isn't that bad for this profile though, and he's walking a ton, so he's basically living up to his scouting report to a T as a low BA slugger

Name: Carlos Lagrange
Report: 99.2 MPH fastball with a 13.1% BB% and 34% whiff%. If the control relegates him to a pen role, he can still be an elite reliever, so I wouldn't even be too upset if that happens

Name: Henry Bolte
Report: 29.6% whiff% isn't that bad, but the 4 degree launch is still super low and the 39.8% Hard Hit% isn't that great. Regardless, he's ripping up Triple-A, he's an elite pure talent, and while I don't think the Athletics are going to pull the plug on Lawrence Butler, that is a path to playing time right now

Name: James Tibbs III
Report: He's turned himself into a low BA, high OBP slugger with a 35% whiff% and 58% Hard Hit%. He's not lifting and pulling a ton, which I don't love and who knows when/if LA ever gives him a shot. Maybe we have to wait for a trade

Name: Charles Davalan
Report: He's a 22 year old college bat in the lower minors, so his not huge tools could play down at higher levels, but he's destroying the level he's at, slashing .296/.389/.541 with 6 homers, 5 steals, and a 10.6/9.7 K%/BB% in 25 games. The contact is elite, he's lifting, and he's running. I still fear he's a 400-500 AB guy with the Dodgers, but I want to bet on this

Name: Devin Fitz-Gerald
Report: Fitz was old for rookie ball and he's not a huge tools guy, so I was reluctant to go too high this off-season, but he's proving the bat is for real at High-A, slashing .293/.435/.511 with 3 homers, 10 steals, and a 16.4/16.4 K%/BB% in 23 games. He's still not a huge tools guy, but the guy can clearly hit

Name: Bryce Rainer
Report: Rainer was who I predicted would be the #1 prospect in baseball by next off-season, and that is already a disaster with a 44% K% and 70 wRC+ in the lower minors. He's never had a pretty swing, but it's even uglier after shoulder surgery. He's still smoking the ball, so, the shoulder is still supercharged ;), but the hit tool ain't, and it's a major concern right now.

Name: Liam Doyle
Report: 7.31 ERA with a 24.7/9.6 K%/BB% in 16 IP at Double-A. Kade Anderson has blown by him in the Doyle vs. Anderson debate. You have to stay patient, but the hope was that he would just overpower minor league hitters, and it's clearly not happening. That deserves a drop

Name: Jonny Farmelo
Report: The hit tool is killing him with a .202 BA and 28.1% K%. The 27% whiff% actually isn't that bad, so there is hope. I want to give him some more time before dropping him further because the upside is still so big

Name: Steele Hall
Report: Sent to rookie ball, and if you want to read the tea leaves, those tea leaves would say Cincy has some concerns about the hit tool. And then he went 0 for 5 with 3 K in his first game (0 for 4 with 0 K in his 2nd game). We're about to see how bad the hit tool is, but there is clearly risk here

Name: Gage Jump
Report: The 95.6 MPH heater looks good with a 32.8% whiff%, but the secondaries haven't been great, and the numbers aren't great either with a 5.64 ERA, 1.61 WHIP and 31.7/13.5 K%/BB% in 22.1 IP.

Name: Jamie Arnold
Report: 4.32 ERA, 1.64 WHIP with a 28.4/9.5 K%/BB% in 25 IP at Double-A. He really hasn't been that great. I'll keep his value steady for now

Name: Gage Wood
Report: Dominating Single-A but it's silly that he's even at Single-A to begin with. Value holds steady for me rather than blowing up

Name: Hagen Smith
Report: 17% BB% at AAA and it's mostly a 2 pitch mix. It's looking very relievery right now, but it's elite reliever potential if he does up there

Name: Esmerlyn Valdez
Report: Pitt got stacked in a hurry, but there is still going to be plenty of opportunity long term, and when Valdez does get that shot, he'll be a low BA slugger

Name: Hector Rodriguez
Report: 16.5/12.0 K%/BB% with 5 homers in 33 games at Triple-A. The raw power isn't huge, but the 43.5% Hard Hit% isn't bad and all this guy has done is hit at every level

Name: Travis Sykora
Report: Underwent TJ in August of 2025 and will very likely miss all of 2026

Name: Jett Williams
Report: 31.1% Hard Hit% at Triple-A isn't going to cut it and it's led to a 93 wRC+ in 32 games. He lift/pulls, he runs, and he gets the bat on the ball, so maybe he can be a Statcast Killa type, but I would really want to see more hard hit balls than that

Name: Cooper Pratt
Report: 84.1 MPH EV with a 87 wRC+ in 25 games at Triple-A. The plate skills are still excellent, he's good on D, and he's young and projectable, so if/when the power comes, everything else is there

Name: Aiva Arquette
Report: Made his season debuted, played two games, and then hasn't placed since April 30th. Not sure what, if anything is going on

Name: Angel Genao
Report: 54.7% GB% and 2 steals in 24 games at Double-A still has me questioning the upside, but the 18.2/20.0 K%/BB% and 131 wRC+ shows the guy can produce with the bat. Better real life bat that fantasy, but he should be good in fantasy too

Name: Caden Scarborough
Report: Yet to debut after undergoing surgery to remove a melanoma

Name: Jefferson Rojas
Report: Rojas' raw and game power are both up with 4 homers and a 31.7% GB% in 18 games at Double-A. The 24.6% whiff% says to not worry about the elevated K rate, and he's hitting well at Double-A with a 136 wRC+. The only oddity is 0 steals, but his trade record says he should start running more

Name: Jacob Reimer
Report: Mediocre at Double-A but he's been heating up of late and he's already played really well at the level last year. Value holds serve

Name: Michael Arroyo
Report: He's now trending towards the OF, and as a corner outfielder, it puts a ton of pressure on his bat

Name: Ike Irish
Report: 51.9% GB% is still on the high side for a slugging corner OF, and he's a college bat at High-A, but he's crushing the level with a 164 wRC+ in 21 games. He's living up to his 19th pick in the draft hype

Name: Arjun Nimmala
Report: Bouncing back from the rough 2nd half at High-A in 2025 with a 132 wRC+, but the .241 BA still shows the lingering hit tool issues

Name: John Gil
Report: He showed the power explosion was coming in spring, and now it's here with 4 homers and a 41.3% GB% in 25 games at High-A. The plate skills and base running are still excellent. I had him as a potential breakout this off-season and the breakout is here

Name: Robert Arias
Report: I've been an Arias fan for a little while now, writing him up several times over the years and writing in his Top 1,000 blurb, "Arias is a future breakout candidate who has a strong foundation of excellent contact skills, a projectable 6’1” frame, CF defense and speed." And now that breakout is here, slashing .337/.433/.517 with 4 homers, 11 steals, and a 15.4/14.4 K%/BB% in 22 games at Single-A. The 50% GB% is still on the high side, but the power uptick is clearly here

Name: Chase Harlan
Report: 19.6/20.6 K%/BB% with a 25.8% whiff% in 22 games at Single-A is great to see. The power will be there. Great start

Name: Kevin Alvarez
Report: Holding his own at Single-A with a 97 wRC+. Lack of walks and high groundball rate shows there is a lot of refinement still needed here

Name: Wandy Asigen
Report: Yet to debut with the DSL season starting in early June I believe

Name: Abimelec Ortiz
Report: Once again hitting really well at Triple-A and the underlying numbers are even better than the surface stats. You have to think he gets a shot soon. He makes for a really good stash now in leagues where he is available

Name: Kahlil Watson
Report: 32.9% whiff% shows the hit tool risk is still there, but with how hard he's crushing the ball (93.6 MPH EV), lifting (22.1 degree launch) and running (9 steals), that actually isn't that bad. The fantasy upside is so fun here, but the hit tool risk is still making me a bit hesitant

Name: Eduardo Tait
Report: Hitting for power at High-A with 5 homers but the hit tool risk is showing with a .233 BA and 34.9% whiff%

Name: Andrew Fischer
Report: 40% whiff% with a 38.6% K% at High-A is extremely concerning. He's hitting homers and performing well, but the hit tool is way worse than hoped for

Name: Kayson Cunningham
Report: The pro debut steered us wrong and his elite hit tool rep is shining through with a 13.2/16.0 K%/BB% in 23 games at Single-A, but it comes with 0 homers and 1 steal. I'm in on hit tool first guys this year though, so the fuck the power/speed I guess hah

Name: Brody Hopkins
Report: 4.88 ERA with a 24.2/20.2 K%/BB% in 27.2 IP in Triple-A. He might have a wee bit of a walk issues. Stuff is still filthy but it's too filthy for it's own good because he has no idea where it's going

Name: Miguel Sime
Report: One of my top FYPD Targets who was a true sleeper, and he's woken everybody up with an upper 90's fastball and whiff machine breakers. It's led to a 3.07 ERA with a 54.2/18.6 K%/BB% in 14.2 IP. As you can see, the control is still a major risk and so is a third pitch. Even if he did end up in the pen though, he could be an elite closer.

Name: Joseph Dzierwa
Report: One of my top FYPD Targets who was getting zero love, Dzierwa is feeling the love now with his fastball up into the mid 90's and him performing well at High-A with a 2.33 ERA and 27.6/6.7 K%/BB% in 27 IP. It's still probably mid rotation upside at peak, so don't want to get too crazy but you know I'm loving this

Name: Juan Sanchez
Report: 12 wRC+ in 14 games at Single-A. Rookie Ball just started. Clearly he's not ready for full season ball so I don't see why they wouldn't demote him

Name: Francisco Renteria
Report: Yet to debut. DSL starts in early June

Name: Angeibel Gomez
Report: Yet to debut. DSL starts in early June

Name: Cooper Ingle
Report: Bo Naylor has a 6 wRC+. I have to think his time is coming up, and Ingle is at Triple-A with a 236 wRC+ in 17 games. He has a 51.7% Hard Hit% and he's always had a good feel to hit. Great pick up right now.

Name: Seaver King
Report: The AFL breakout has rolled over into Double-A, slashing .306/.408/.561 with 5 homers, 3 steals, and a 21.5/14.9 K%/BB% in 25 games. The 38.9% GB% is way down. He's been caught stealing 6 times, which I think is an aberration looking at his career, but it's worth pointing out. Either way, he's back on track to being what he thought he was when Washington took him 10th overall

Name: Karson Milbrandt
Report: 1.85 ERA with a 32.0/10.3 K%/BB% in 24.1 IP at Double-A. I liked Milbrandt a lot this off-season, the stuff is really good from the left side, and he's now conquering Double-A. He's underrated

Name: Kyson Witherspoon
Report: He didn't miss as many bats as optimal in college, and now he's struggling at High-A with a 7.06 ERA and 25.3/13.1 K%/BB% in 21.2 IP at High-A. It's still a small sample and we have to give him more time to get comfortable, but it's a pretty discouraging start

Name: Jaxon Wiggins
Report: Hit the IL with right elbow inflammation after 2 starts. Just the life of a flamethrowing pitching prospect

Name: TJ Nichols
Report: Hit the IL after 1 start with an undisclosed injury. Hopefully it's not an arm injury but I have no idea

Name: Tanner McDougal
Report: The 98.4 MPH fastball isn't actually missing many bats with a 22.4% whiff%, but the secondaries are, and he has a 34.9% whiff%. He's pitching well at Triple-A, but there is still relief risk with a high walk rate and with barely going to the change. And now there is injury risk too with him down with a forearm strain

Name: Raudi Rodriguez
Report: Skipped over High-A and went from Single-A in 2025 to Double-A in 2026 and he's having no issues, slashing .270/.430/.382 with 3 homers, 11 steals, and a 18.3/20.0 K%/BB% in 26 games. The plate skills are transferring to say the least. He ripped up the AFL too. He's a good athlete who hits the ball hard and has speed. He's a great pickup right now if he's out there in your league

Name: Deniel Ortiz
Report: They started him at Double-A, which was a big sign of confidence, but he immediately went down with a wrist injury

Name: Felnin Celesten
Report: Quietly having a good season with a 125 wRC+ in 24 games at High-A but it comes with only 1 homer and a high groundball rate. He looks like more a slow burn than a rocket ship

Name: Nate George
Report: Homer power has yet to come with 1 homer and a 50.8% GB% in 20 games at High-A, but everything else looks good

Name: Cris Rodriguez
Report: Stateside rookie is just getting started and he hasn't done much in 3 games yet

Name: Johenssy Colome
Report: Yet to debut. DSL starts in early June

Name: Santiago Solarte
Report: Yet to debut. DSL starts in early June

Name: Braylon Doughty
Report: 2.76 ERA with a 23.2/2.9 K%/BB% in 16.1 IP at High-A. He's going control over big K rate, which is fine by me if the control is in the elite range. The stuff is good. The org is good. I like him

Name: Johnny King
Report: 0.63 ERA with a 38.6/15.8 K%/BB% in 14.1 IP at High-A. Love the talent and filth from the left side, but clearly there is still plenty of rawness here

Name: Blake Burke
Report: Slashing .237/.328/.551 with 9 homers, 11 steals, and a 26.1/10.4 K%/BB% in 28 games at Double-A. He's a fun/weird one. He crushes the ball, the lift/pull is up this year, and he's running. There is hit tool risk and lack of defensive value, but he might be the pole position for Milwaukee's 1B of the future job. It's still going to be a dog fight for the job though

Name: Bo Davidson
Report: 26.6% whiff% at Double-A is great to see because that means the hit tool is completely transferring. He's also got 5 dingers. I still hate that he's going to hit in SF, and he's still on the older side, but he's doing what I wanted to see in the upper minores

Name: Sean Keys
Report: Conquering Double-A with 9 homers and a 174 wRC+, but I still do have some concerns on the hit tool on the MLB level with a 26.7% K%. The power looks very legit though

Name: Aroon Escobar
Report: Solid at Double-A with a 105 wRC+. The hit tool is transferring with a 15.3/11.0 K%/BB% which is great to see. Overall it's an encouraging start

Name: Devin Taylor
Report: Ripping up High-A which is expected for him but still great to see. The upper minors will be his first real test, but all this dude does is rake

Name: Josh Adamczewski
Report: Destroying High-A with a 163 wRC+ and 7 homers. Plate skills, raw power and game power all looks great. He's at the least a rock solid MLB bat, and if he keeps this up at Double-A, I will up that projection

Name: Marco Dinges
Report: We've seen him rip up High-A already and he's doing it again. I really like his bat, but want to see what it looks like in the upper minors before getting too crazy

Name: Demetrio Crisantes
Report: Yet to debut with a hamstring injury

Name: William Bergolla Jr.
Report: Hasn't played since April 9th with a shin bruise, but he was doing his elite contact/speed thing before going down with the injury. Lack of impact could be a problem in truly locking down a full time job with an increasingly crowded Chicago

Name: Kendall George
Report: Everything is transferring to Double-A but the problem is still impact with 0 homers and a .429 BABIP doing a lot of the heavy lifting. If he gets on the field though, he will make a major impact in steals

Name: Wei-En Lin
Report: Everything is transferring to the upper minors, which is a big step, with a 1.61 ERA and 28.9/7.9 K%/BB% in 28 IP. The velocity isn't big but seeing the stuff dominate upper minors hitters is huge

Name: Edwin Arroyo
Report: He held his own at Double-A coming off shoulder surgery, and now he's excelling at Triple-A, slashing .305/.386/.489 with 4 homers, 5 steals, and a 17.5/10.6 K%/BB% in 32 games. The 89.3 MPH EV ain't bad either with lift/pull and speed. He profiles as a potentially solid across the board fantasy player.

Name: Jack Wenninger
Report: He's pitching well at Triple-A, but I'm not overly impressed by the 93.9 MPH velocity, 26.8% whiff%, and 41.1% Hard Hit%. I think he's your classic mid rotation upside starter, which isn't super unique, but still good

Name: Ben Hess
Report: Hit the IL after only 2 outings with arm fatigue

Name: Riley Quick
Report: Quick was a Ben Hess/Brandon Sproat type FYPD Target for me, meaning big guys with bug stuff who didn't have a huge Junior year but who could breakout in pro ball. And now Quick is breaking out in pro ball with a 1.13 ERA and 42.1/7.0 K%/BB% in 16 IP at Single-A and High-A. Obviously it's a small sample and the lower minors, but it's a good sign that pro breakout is coming

Name: Owen Murphy
Report: Getting hit up in the upper minors and without big stuff, he really needs the production to be there. Still a small sample, but rough start

Name: Tyson Lewis
Report: 80 wRC+ with a 39.5% whiff% and 50.8% GB% in 26 games at Single-A. He's just so raw still

Name: Brock Wilken
Report: My dream of him being a 3B seems to be dying. And as a 1B only, there is just so much competition in Milwaukee there long term

Name: Kemp Alderman
Report: 36.6% whiff% with a 97.1 MPH EV says it all. This dude smashes it, but the hit tool risk is high, he's not a big lift/pull guy, and his walk rates in the minors have only been okay. If/when he gets his shot though, the dude is going to rip the ball though

Name: Jonathon Long
Report: Not crushing Triple-A but he's already conquered this level and hit/power combo looks good. He's just waiting on his shot, which may or may not ever come hah ... at least in the near future

Name: Marek Houston
Report: 3 homers in 26 games at High-A isn't blowing the doors off, but it shows he can hit some out with wood bats too, and the hit tool and speed are also there. Solid debut

Name: Staryln Caba
Report: Traded contact for power at High-A by bringing his GB% way down, but the whiff% spiked up with it. He had some hit tool to spare though and the 121 wRC+ at High-A looks good. Overall, I like the attempt to add power. Good start, and his glove will get him on the field eventually

Name: Asbel Gonzalez
Report: Power is up at High-A with 3 homers and he's hitting well with a 131 wRC+. The K rate is up, but the whiff rate isn't, and of course he's running with 15 steals. Strong start

Name: Daniel Pierce
Report: 31.4/5.7 K%/BB% in 17 games at Single-A shows there is a lot of risk here, but he's showing the talent too with 3 homers, 4 steals, and a 102 wRC+. Value holds serve

Name: Gavin Fien
Report: 47.4% K% with a .118 BA in 19 games at Single-A. It's probably too easy to blame the batting stance that I didn't like. But either way, clearly there is major hit tool risk and I feel good about my FYPD ranking of him this off-season by not going too high. Let's give him a bigger sample to get comfortable though before a larger drop

Name: Enrique Bradfield
Report: He was actually hitting the ball much much harder at Triple-A with a 51.6% Hard Hit% and 2 homers in 13 games, although he wasn't hitting well overall with a 91 wRC+ and now he's on the IL with a hand injury. I'm intrigued by the hard hit though

Name: Braden Nett
Report: Just made his debut from a rotator cuff injury and the big stuff is all the way. He also pitched well. He's an upside proximity play "sleeper" that could make for a really good pick up right now in the right leagues

Name: Cole Carrigg
Report: Hitting well at Triple-A but the .436 BABIP is doing a lot of the heavy lifting. He's making a lot of contact, but he had to sacrifice lift/pull to do it. Value is holding steady right now as a fun upside proximity play, but I'm still not completely sold

Name: Blaze Jordan
Report: Contact/power profile is thriving at Triple-A with 8 homers, 46.3% Hard Hit%, and a 12.5 K%. He's not walking and the GB% is very high, so it's still the type of profile that has to fight for it's life on the MLB level. But hard to argue with that hit/power combo. Interesting proximity play

Name: Michael Forret
Report: 1.75 ERA with a 24.7/13.4 K%/BB% in 25.2 IP. I'm a K/BB guy, so I'm more discouraged than encouraged. I'm starting to think the upside just isn't that high here

Name: Luis Perales
Report: 4.56 ERA with a 20.2/12.8 K%/BB% in 25.2 IP at AAA. The stuff is still huge, so I want to keep betting on the stuff, but those results are making it as hard as possible. The odds of him ending up in the pen are rising, but this is really his first full year back from TJ, so let's have some patience

Name: Luis De Leon
Report: The inevitable explosion for the fire balling lefty turned out to be not so inevitable with a 6.26 ERA and 25.9/14.8 K%/BB% in 23 IP at Double-A. Give him some time to get hot and find a groove, but his value certainly isn't rising

Name: David Shields
Report: 2.70 ERA with a 33.7/8.7 K%/BB% in 26.2 IP at High-A. A Parker Messick like peak is the hope here

Name: Joshua Kuroda-Grauer
Report: I would have sworn I had Grauer on the off-season rankings, but obviously not (not sure if I erased him by accident maybe). Either way, he's on these rankings for his elite contact (9.8% K%), increased power (6 homers) and speed (10 steals) in 28 games at Double-A. He still might end up a utility guy, but the Athletics are a perfect org for a guy like this to actually get a shot.

Name: Tommy Troy
Report: Once again showing off a nice across the board profile at Triple-A, but it's not high upside, and it seems like Airzona is treating him as a future super utility player

Name: Luke Adams
Report: Hasn't played since April 11th for reasons I am unsure of. His value was holding steady before that, but a 85.5 MPH EV is just not going to cut it for a 1B. Need to see a bigger sample though

Name: Xavier Isaac
Report: Isaac is back to being a power hitting machine coming off brain surgery with 7 homers in 21 games at Double-A, but the 48.6% whiff% and 39.5% K% is way too high. The 25.6% BB% is also very high, but that swing and miss is in beyond the danger zone. The hope is that that comes down because how could we not give him a ton of leeway for brain surgery. It's just amazing he's back out there

Name: Roldy Brito
Report: He's hitting well at Single-A with a 120 wRC+ in 23 games, but I still don't love the 51.4% GB% and 29.2% whiff% combo. He's rising, but I don't want to go too crazy

Name: Jaison Chourio
Report: Bouncing back at High-A, slashing .317/.431/.476 with 2 homers, 10 steals, and a 17.6/17.6 K%/BB% in 22 games. This is what we expected last year, and while he's getting a bump, the hope that this is a superstar rocket ship is still waning for me.

Name: Blake Mitchell
Report: 42.5% whiff% with a .206 BA at High-A shows this is major hit tool risk, but the power is back as expected with 6 homers, he runs with 5 steals, and he gets on base with a 31.7% BB%. I still think he can be a super fun fantasy catcher, especially in OBP leagues.

Name: Billy Carlson
Report: 82 wRC+ in 24 games is feeding into that this is a glove first player without big offensive upside

Name: Nick Becker
Report: Starting in rookie ball, which is not a big vote of confidence, but he's hit well in 3 games, albeit with a 30% K%, so maybe he can quickly get to full season ball

Name: Tanner Franklin
Report: The transition from the pen into a starter has mostly been a success, but he's hit a few road bumps recently. Big stuff, but I still think the bullpen risk is very high with a 4.19 ERA and 33.3/11.1 K%/BB% in 19.1 IP at High-A

Name: Gage Stanifer
Report: 7.71 ERA with a 30.7/18.2 K%/BB% in 18.2 IP at Double-A. Double-A gave him trouble last year too in a small sample. The upper minors are slowing him down

Name: Jimmy Crooks
Report: 34.5% K% and 36.6% whiff% still has me skeptical if the bat will play on the MLB level, but he's killing it with 10 homers in 25 games, and the Cardinals current catcher job is still a bit up in the air

Name: Wehiwa Aloy
Report: 27.6/8.6 K%/BB% in 22 games at High-A shows the risk is still present, but he's conquering the level with 6 homers and a 130 wRC+. What he does in the upper minors will be the big test

Name: Kane Kepley
Report: Hit/speed profile is completely transferring to High-A but he's yet to hit a homer and we need to see it in the upper minors

Name: Aaron Walton
Report: He's a college bat I thought was underrated and now he's ripping up High-A, slashing .292/.388/.528 with 4 homers, 8 steals, and a 25.0/8.7 K%/BB% in 24 games. We need to see it in the upper minors, but love the start

Name: Coy James
Report: Coy James was billed as hit tool first but he's performing the opposite of that, slashing .198/.355/.372 with 4 homers, 12 steals, and a 28.0/17.8 K%/BB% in 24 games. That BA is likely bad luck, but the 31.3% whiff% says it's not all bad luck. I'm more encouraged than discouraged really

Name: Blaine Bullard
Report: Bullard got $1.7 million in the draft as a projectable and toolsy high school bat, and now he's showing off the upside at Single-A, slashing .230/.337/.425 with 4 homers, 16 steals, and a 32.4/10.5 K%/BB% in 23 games. You can see the hit tool risk, but the 28% whiff% isn't bad at all. I really like Bullard, and if some of the buzzier FYPD breakouts are already gone, jump on Bullard

Name: Colby Shelton
Report: Here is what I wrote about Shelton in the latest Dynasty Baseball Rundown, "Colby Shelton is an interesting one for my deep leaguers out there. Not only interesting, but super weird. This dude hit 25 homers with a 1.148 OPS and 24.6% K% in his first year in the SEC in 2023. So I'm saying this guy can clearly rake. He hit 20 homers in 2024 and then in 2025 he decided to aim for contact over power, and he did it easily with a 11.8% K% and .377 BA in his senior year. Being able to bring your contact rates down that much again just shows there is something special in his bat. He's now at High-A, and he's destroying the level, slashing .378/.485/.720 with 6 homers, 5 steals, and a 18.2/15.2 K%/BB% in 22 games. It sure looks like he's now combining the improved hit with his legit power. He's already 23 years old, he's not a great athlete and he's a 2B, but I think he's worth keeping an eye on."

Name: Henry Godbout
Report: The Red Sox did it again, finding power from an elite contact guy. Godbout has 4 homers with a 41.4% GB% and 12.8% whiff% in 20 games at High-A. It's still not high upside and it still might not be an MLB starter, but good start to his pro career

Name: Ethan Pecko
Report: Pecko had a late start to the season with what I'm assuming is the "good" thoracic outlet syndrome, and he's looked completely healthy since returning with a 1.80 ERA and 30.4/8.7 K%/BB% in 5 IP Triple-A. He was good for 8 IP at Single-A too in his rehab outings. The fastball is averaging 94.9 MPH and the cutter and slider are missing bats. He pitched well in the upper minors last year too. The stuff is more solid than standout, so I'm not really targeting him, but he's a good proximity arm

Name: Charlee Soto
Report: Yet to debut coming off biceps/bone spur injury/surgery. Injury risk is sky high here but the talent is huge assuming full health

Name: Christian Zazueta
Report: 3.13 xFIP, 4.18 ERA, and a 37.9/6.3 K%/BB% in 23.2 IP at High-A. The stuff is really good with a plus fastball/changeup combo as the moneymaker, but I want to see it in the upper minors first before going higher than this

Name: Anderson Brito
Report: 9.5% BB% isn't and he's pitching well at High-A with a 3.86 ERA and 31% K% in 18.2 IP. Any signs of control improvement is a good sign because the stuff is nasty

Name: Khal Stephen
Report: 2.93 ERA with a 30.4/13.9 K%/BB% in 27.2 IP at Double-A. The elite walk rates from the lower minors are not translating to the upper minors. The 26.7% whiff% isn't as high as the K rate. I still think he's a mid rotation upside type, which is good, but not a super valuable dynasty asset

Name: Kash Mayfield
Report: 2.29 ERA with a 30.7/16.0 K%/BB% in 19.2 IP at High-A. A Noah Cameron outcome is what you are hoping for here, but he can easily end up a back end guy

Name: Cameron Cauley
Report: 100 wRC+ at Triple-A says it all. He's been okay. Not kicking the door down. I'll keep his value steady

Name: Joseph Sullivan
Report: Doing exactly at Double-A what he did in the upper minors, which is show a great power/speed combo with major hit tool risk. It feels like another super toolsy Houston prospect who doesn't hit enough to be a true full time player

Name: David Davalillo
Report: 3.86 ERA with a 33.3/7.4 K%/BB% in 23.1 IP at Double-A. The stuff isn't big, but he keeps producing everywhere he goes

Name: Termarr Johnson
Report: Tanking at Triple-A with a 41 wRC+, 27.7% Hard Hit% and 30% whiff%. Disaster. He already wasn't an upside guy, and now he's not a production guy either. Still early, and he's not this bad but I'm super discouraged

Name: Dante Nori
Report: Everything is transferring to Double-A except the walk rate, and the power it up a bit too. The Phillies strategy of taking older high school bats might pay off again.

Name: Ethan Petry
Report: Destroying High-A which isn't very surprising. The upper minors is his real first test

Name: Marconi German
Report: Yet to debut and with stateside rookie ball starter, maybe there is an injury here?

Name: Dillon Lewis
Report: Hitting .220 with a 31.1% K% at Double-A. The hit tool is killing him, which is why the Yanks were willing to trade him away. The power/speed is good though and the 30.9% whiff% isn't terrible, so the upside is still high

Name: Luke Dickerson
Report: He's repeating Single-A as a 20 year old and the 29.8% K% still shows the major hit too risk, but he's hitting well with a 124 wRC+, so I'll keep his value steady

Name: Dorian Soto
Report: Rookie ball is just getting started and he's been hitting well in the early going

Name: Ching-Hsien Ko
Report: Slashing .288/.434/.576 with 4 homers and a 23.7/18.4 K%/BB% in 17 games at Single-A. The GB% is down. He's bouncing back from a rough Single-A stint in 2025 and he's still age appropriate for the level

Name: Slater de Brun
Report: Yet to debut with a wrist injury

Name: Diego Tornes
Report: Yet to debut

Name: Caden Bodine
Report: Destroying Single-A with 4 homers and a 3.5/9.7 K%/BB% in 24 games. It's only Single-A, but still, that is just true obliteration. Him and Flewelling are going to be a fun catcher duo climbing the minors together. I can see a path where both are impact fantasy catchers

Name: Tommy White
Report: 55.7% GB% with low walk rates are going to be a problem for playing time, but with the Athletics, it's not as big of a deal. The contact/raw power combo has translated to every level, and if/when he gets his shot in the bigs, he could be a fantasy relevant bat. Lack of launch and speed does still cap the upside

Name: Miguel Ullola
Report: 15.9% BB% at Triple-A. His control issues are seemingly going to have him end up in the pen

Name: Jonathan Santucci
Report: 5.57 ERA with a 34.8/19.1 K%/BB% in 21 IP at Double-A. I'll keep his value steady as a standard mid rotation upside guy, but right now, back end looks more accurate

Name: Ty Johnson
Report: Yet to debut with a lower back strain

Name: Kruz Schoolcraft
Report: The stuff did tick up like I expected post draft, but the production isn't there at all with a 13.50 ERA and 19.4/21.0 K%/BB% in 10.2 IP at Single-A. Clearly he's super raw. He might deserve an even bigger drop than this

Name: Nelson Rada
Report: 11.8% Hard Hit% at Triple-A is ridiculous and it's resulted in a 83 wRC+ in 23 games. The profile remains the same, but the hard hit is going in the wrong direction

Name: Jace LaViolette
Report: We knew there was hit tool risk, but a 43.1% whiff% and 41.7% K% is just on the absolute worst end of it. He's still so talented that I want to give him more time to get comfortable in pro ball to see if those can drop at least into the mid 30's

Name: Luke Stevenson
Report: Back to dominating High-A but he's still not hitting a ton of homers with only 2. I have to think the homers will come, but we have to see it in the upper minors, and he's still blocked

Name: Ramon Ramirez
Report: Hitting well at High-A. He continues to quietly be a really good lower minors catcher prospect

Name: Axiel Plaz
Report: 143 wRC+ in 23 games at High-A, and while a lot of that is BABIP induced (.429), it still points towards Plaz being one of the more underrated catching prospects in the lower minors

Name: Cam Cannarella
Report: Fractured his wrist after just 7 games at High-A. They were an exciting 7 games though with elite plate skills and a 155 wRC+. It was only the lower minors, but great sign the profile will transfer to pro ball

Name: Sean Gamble
Report: 32.7% K% with a .104 BA is showing major hit tool risk. .153 BABIP shows he's been extremely unlucky, but it's not all bad luck. The dude has a 7 wRC+ in 26 games. I'll stay a bit more patient because you have to let these kids get comfortable, but pretty discouraging

Name: Bruin Agbayani
Report: The most underrated man alive one of my favorite deep FYPD targets is back to doing his elite plate skill thing at Single-A with a 5.4/18.9 K%/BB% in 5 games. We need a bigger sample, but love it so far. I want to remain high on him

Name: Ricky Tiedemann
Report: Another setback coming back from TJ once again delayed the start of his season, but he's supposedly back on the comeback trail. I'm starting to lose hope, but I mean, if he gets healthy, and starts throwing fire again, the hype can pick up quickly. A pen role is also seeming more and more likely even if he does get back healthy, at least early in his career

Name: Santiago Suarez
Report: 6.41 ERA (3.70 xFIP) with a 29.9/6.9 K%/BB% in 19.2 IP at Double-A. I'm a K/BB guy, so I lean more towards it being encouraging but I wouldn't completely dismiss the ERA. His stuff is hittable

Name: Christian Oppor
Report: 8.04 ERA with a 13.3/22.9 K%/BB% in 15.2 IP at Double-A. Talented arm, but the upper minors are destroying him

Name: Nate Payne
Report: Payne is a 6'3'' lefty with a smooth delivery and a plus low to mid 90's fastball as his moneymaker that misses a ton of bats despite not huge velocity. The curve is nice looking pitch with plus potential and he also throws a cutter, slider and change. He's been a strikeout machine in the lower minors with a 40.8% K%. I like him

Name: Winston Santos
Report: 10.80 ERA with a 28.3/9.4 K%/BB% in 10 IP at Double-A. He's not pitching well but clearly there is bad luck in play too as the K/BB isn't bad at all. I'll give him some more time before a bigger drop

Name: Bishop Letson
Report: I think I was the only person pumping the brakes on Letson, writing, "I try to stop myself from getting too amped up about "a looks the part" dream build. Maybe that is the Moneyball generation in me, but I do still think it can seep too much into scouting. I remember when I pumped the brakes on Darren Bowen back in 2023 because I thought he was getting too much of the "looks great in the uniform bump." Now, I like Letson a lot more than Bowen, but I want to see a bit more against advanced competition before really going crazy." ... and now he is facing that advanced competition and getting rocked with a 7.23 ERA and 19.8/16.5 K%/BB% in 18.2 IP. Let him get comfortable, but I feel good about my off-season evaluation

Name: JT Quinn
Report: Here is what I wrote about Quinn in the Rundowns last week and my thoughts remain the same, "I wasn't on JT Quinn, but you damn right I'm on him now after yet another strong outing, going 5 IP with 3 hits, 0 ER, and a 5/2 K/BB at High-A. He now has a 2.70 ERA with a 26.7/5.6 K%/BB% in 23.1 IP. Just like Sime and Quick, Quinn is also a big man at 6'6'', 210 pounds who throws hard with mid 90's heat. He combines the heat with a pair of vicious breakers. He has to show it at higher levels and he didn't show this level of control in college, so I'm not going crazy for him yet, but he's definitely a big riser."

Name: AJ Russell
Report: The Rangers took the TJ discount on Russell at 52nd overall and they are easing him into things at Single-A with 2 IP outings. There has been some good (41% K%) and some bad (12.8% BB% with  5.00 ERA in 9 IP). He's a big dude with big stuff, so I like to bet on those types, but we need a bigger sample at higher levels

Name: Jared Thomas
Report: Yet to debut with a fractured hamate

Name: Dasan Hill
Report: 8.44 ERA with a 31.6/17.1 K%/BB% in 16 IP at High-A. He's still clearly super raw with major control risk

Name: David Hagaman
Report: He had small sample success in 2025 that he isn't repeating in 2026. But it's just 7.2 IP and his season got a late start, so let's see a bigger sample before making bigger moves

Name: Jose Corniell
Report: Yet to debut with a dead arm. He just came back from TJ in 2025. Pitching prospects are a nightmare

Name: Kevin Defrank
Report: I think the word is that his season is done with an elbow injury. The life of a flamethrowing teenager is just brutal

Name: Gavin Kilen
Report: 110 wRC+ with 2 homers and 0 steals in 26 games at High-A. I just don't see an impact fantasy bat here

Name: Ryan Wideman
Report: Off to a strong start at Single-A and best of all is showing a good hit tool with a 19.9% whiff%, but Single-A is just way too low of a level to get too excited yet. He's a big dude and a great athlete, so the value is rising, but we really need to see it at higher levels.

Name: Landon Harmon
Report: 1.88 ERA with a 21.2/9.6 K%/BB% in 14.1 IP at Single-A. I'm a K/BB guy so more discouraged than encouraged by the start, but I'll hold his value steady

Name: Argenis Cayama
Report: 3.09 ERA with a 33.3/1.1 K%/BB% in 23.1 IP at Single-A. He had a 10.3% BB% last year, so the control is taking a huge jump. He was one of the best pitchers in rookie ball, and now he's one of the best pitchers in Single-A. He sits low 90's, so it's not huge stuff, but the sinker is nasty, so it works

Name: Jeral Perez
Report: Been terrible at High-A but a lot of it looks like bad luck so want to give him a bigger sample

Name: Cole Mathis
Report: Mathis underwent Tommy John surgery shortly after being drafted in 2024 and it messed up his 2025 season, but he looked good in the AFL, and now he's ripping up the lower minors. He's has to show it in the upper minors first, and he's a righty 1B, so it's going to be a nightmare to get on the field. Jonathan Long is still waiting ahead of him

Name: Samuel Zavala
Report: Zavala was a favorite of mine in what feels like 100 years ago, but he's still only 21 years old, and now he's playing really well at Double-A, slashing .265/.409/.461 with 5 homers, 5 steals, and a 19.7/19.7 K%/BB% in 27 games. It's not the highest upside profile, but the plate approach is so mature

Name: Jaden Fauske
Report: 128 wRC+ in 26 games at Single-A. It only comes with 1 homer and a 52.6% GB%, but the approach is mature with a 30.0/19.2 K%/BB%. The 25.9% whiff% looks good. I had him as a really good, probably better in real life than fantasy bat, and that is still how I have him

Name: Cam Collier
Report: The groundball rate is down and he's hitting more homers but he's still not hitting that well at Double-A. His bat has a very high bar to clear and it just hasn't be clearing it

Name: Aidan Smith
Report: His season is just getting started as he returns from a hammy

Name: Brendan Tunink
Report: Looked great for 8 games at Single-A with the hit tool transferring before hitting the IL. He's a tooled up guy, so the start was exciting

Name: Murf Gray
Report: He's ripping up Single-A but he's far too young for that level to get too crazy. I really liked his size/contact/power profile in FYPD's, and I did give him a solid ranking, but the same reasons I didn't go higher are still there, which is that he might end up a righty 1B, and it's going to a battle to get on the field

Name: Wyatt Sanford
Report: Hitting really well at High-A but the 37.3% K% and 39.5% whiff% are just way way way too high

Name: Aidan West
Report: Just made his debut in rookie ball and cracked a double in his first game. Fun high upside Dodgers play

Name: Owen Carey
Report: Performing well as a 19 year old at High-A with a hit tool first profile (14% K%). He's been out for a few weeks for reasons I am unsure of

Name: Yeremy Cabrera
Report: Yeremy has been on the Top 500 before and was a just missed last year, but he's back on now with him crushing Single-A, slashing .316/.443/.653 with 7 homers, 16 steals, and a 25.4/18.0 K%/BB% in 26 games. He's repeating the level and is almost 21 years old, so I need to see it at higher levels, but he deserves to get on the list

Name: Enddy Azocar
Report: Breaking out at Single-A, slashing .282/.333/.509 with 5 homers, 5 steals, and a 23.3/6.7 K%/BB% in 26 games. He's a projectable 6'2'' with a vicious righty swing. There is still rawness here as you can see with the K/BB, but there is fun upside in there too

Name: Ryan Mitchell
Report: Hit tool is way worse than expected with a 39.8% K% and .169 BA in 22 games at Single-A. 34.2% whiff% isn't quite as bad, but clearly this is a major issue

Name: Yairo Padilla
Report: Yet to debut with a shoulder strain

Name: Edgar Montero
Report: 40% K%, 39.8% whiff% and 26 wRC+ in 14 games at Single-A. This is why I like to have some caution on DSL repeaters. He's still tooled up and we have to give him some time to adjust, so don't want to kill him yet

Name: Luis Cova
Report: DSL repeater who is striking out a ton in the very early going of rookie ball. Let's get a bigger sample

Name: Patrick Forbes
Report: Yet to debut with a flexor strain

Name: Briggs McKenzie
Report: Yet to debut

Name: Michael Oliveto
Report: Yet to debut with a broken toe

Name: Emanuel Luna
Report: DSL starts in early June. Yet to debut

Name: Angel Nunez Jr.
Report: DSL starts in early June. Yet to debut

Name: Elian Rosario
Report: DSL starts in early June. Yet to debut

Name: Tyson Hardin
Report: 2.82 xFIP (6.66 ERA) with a 33.3/8.3 K%/BB% in 25.2 IP at Double-A. The ERA is still a tad high, but I love seeing the strikeouts against advanced competition. I've never been the high guy on Hardin and I still think he's a back end guy, but I'll give him the Milwaukee bump with the strong K/BB

Name: Bryce Mayer
Report: 3.86 ERA with a 39.7/9.0 K%/BB% in 18.2 IP at Double-A. The Astros aren't producing the rabbits out of their hats as much of late, but Mayer is that type without nasty stuff but strong production.

Name: Yhoiker Fajardo
Report: 1.46 ERA with a 33.3/2.9 K%/BB% in 24.2 IP at High-A. The stuff is still more solid than truly nasty, but no stops in the lower minors have been able to slow him down yet

Name: Matt Wilkenson
Report: When you don't have big stuff, it's huge to see it in the upper minors, and Wilkenson is showing it in the upper minors with a 1.14 ERA and 34.1/8.0 K%/BB% in 23.2 IP. The fastball barely gets into the low 90's but hitters struggle with it, and he has a solid slider and change. There is quite clearly mid rotation upside in here, velocity be damned

Name: Alejandro Rosario
Report: Finally got TJ in January 2026 when it was announced he would need it in February 2025. Better late than never I guess. He was looking like a legit top of the rotation starter when healthy, so while it seems the odds of him getting back to that aren't super high, he's worth this ranking to see what happens

Name: Aaron Watson
Report: Debuting him in rookie ball, and while it's not a great assignment, I don't mind letting these high school break in as easy as possible to pro ball. He also pitched well in the first game. He's an underrated arm

Name: Jose Mejia
Report: He's old for Single-A, but it's still great to see his elite plate skills transferring with a 16.3/21.2 K%/BB% and 172 wRC+ in 26 games. And he's got a good looking righty swing and there is definitely some pop in the bat with 3 homers. He's shaping up to be a really good all round hitter

Name: Tai Peete
Report: 35.6% whiff% and 30.7/9.6 K%/BB% at High-A shows the hit tool risk is still likely to tank him, but the upside is showing too with 4 homers, 4 steals, and a 129 wRC+ in 23 games

Name: Slade Caldwell
Report: .139 BA with a 32% whiff% is just not going to cut it for this profile. Some of it is bad luck and he's still getting on base and running, but I don't like this start at all

Name: Khristian Curtis
Report: 4.01 xFIP (5.33 ERA) with a 33.0/7.3 K%/BB% in 25.1 IP at Double-A. He's a big dude with big stuff and a starter's pitch mix. The K/BB looks great. Pitt has another good one

Name: Chase Shores
Report: I still lean on him ending up in the bullpen, but he's showing off his upside in a starting role with a 3.69 xFIP (5.06 ERA) and a 34.3/13.4 K%/BB% in 16 IP at High-A. He's a huge dude with huge stuff, so why not bet on the upside at this point, and he can be a potentially back end bullpen arm if he can't start

Name: Bryce Cunningham
Report: His season is just getting started and he's pitched well in 2 outings at High-A. Just gotta wait for him to get to higher levels

Name: Zach Root
Report: He's been out after just 5 IP for reasons I am unsure of. He wasn't pitching particularly well but the stuff and looked and it's obviously only 5 IP.

Name: Cam Leiter
Report: The Dodgers took the shoulder surgery discount on Leiter and he's looked good in 10.2 IP at Single-A with a 3.38 ERA and 42.9/9.5 K%/BB%. They are obviously going to super slow play him, and while I love the Dodgers developing him, I hate that it's impossible to crack that rotation

Name: Kelvis Salcedo
Report: He got a late start to the season but he's ramping up now at Single-A and he's pitched really well in 2 outings. He's a "doesn't look the part" discount guy who I like, but man, he really doesn't look the part

Name: Yordanny Monegro
Report: I was ready for battle. Me against the entire prospect world. I had the baseball bat I keep next to my bed because a home intruder could never defeat a guy with a baseball bat. I had a kitchen knife. And I had a screwdriver. That's basically all the weapons I have in my house. I was ready to defend Yordanny's honor against all doubters... and then he went down with a UCL injury that required Tommy John surgery that could knock him out for all of 2026 or close to it ... No. Not like this. This is isn't how I wanted to go out. And I hate to say it, but he's not quite good enough to really take the Tommy John discount on. Hold him for free, sure. Pick him up at the end of this season or in the next off-season, sure. But this is brutal. At full health, Monegro dominated with a secondary first profile, going to his plus slider the most. He also uses a plus curve and a bat missing changeup. Off those secondaries he mixed in a mid 90's sinker and 4-seamer. The fastballs aren't as good, which is why a lot of the prospect world was out, but I mean, it surely worked at Double-A with a 2.67 ERA and 35.8/5.8 K%/BB% in 33.2 IP before going down with the injury. I was ready to bet on the unique-ish profile and bet on fastball improvement over time, but coming off Tommy John. I'm way less gung ho about it

Name: Juan Valera
Report: Valera would have been a Top 100 prospect if he didn't go down with another elbow injury that required Tommy John. Brutal, but unfortunately, not surprising. His upside is high enough to not completely write off, but I'm not exactly going after him

Name: LuJames Groover
Report: The plate skills are at least plus, and he's knocking on the door of the bigs but there is just little power or speed. Solid bat is the ceiling

Name: Max Anderson
Report: He went down with a quad strain early in the season and is on the rehab trail now.

Name: Gabriel Gonzalez
Report: 8 homers with solid contact rates in 32 games at Triple-A. He has a .182 BA, and while lot of that seems like bad luck with a .170 BABIP, it's not all bad luck with a 31.2% Hard Hit%. He's a decent proximity bat

Name: Roc Riggio
Report: .229 BA with a 31.3% K% in 27 games at Double-A. The whiff rate isn't that bad, but as an older guy at Double-A, he needs to rake, and he's not raking

Name: Brandon Compton
Report: Hitting well at High-A but the 32.9% K% and 42.5% whiff% is just too extreme, especially in the lower minors

Name: Alex Clemmey
Report: 21.6% BB% in 19.2 IP at Double-A. Control issues are out of  ... control

Name: Esteban Mejia
Report: 6.27 ERA with a 24.7% BB% in 18.2 IP at Single-A. The stuff is great but obviously he's still quite raw

Name: Jurrangelo Cijntje
Report: Not pitching well at Double-A at all. The stuff is big, but it's just not coming together in pro ball for him

Name: Ethan Frey
Report: I'm happy I showed some restraint on Frey's 2025 pro debut with him struggling at High-A this year with a 58 wRC+ in 22 games. The hit tool and groundballs are why I was a bit cautious, and both of those things have been a problem

Name: Jake Munroe
Report: Munroe is a guy I wrote up earlier in the season as an underrated college bat with a hit/power combo that is transferring to High-A with 4 homers, a 159 wRC+ and 17.8/12.9 K%/BB% in 23 games. I want to see what he can do when he gets the upper minors.

Name: Mitch Bratt
Report: Looking like a back end starter at Triple-A

Name: Jadher Areinamo
Report: 6 homers with a .172 BA in 14 games at Double-A, but the .105 BABIP points towards major poor luck

Name: Aron Estrada
Report: Struggling at Double-A but he hit well there last year and want to give him some time to get hot

Name: Yophery Rodriguez
Report: Yophery was mediocre at best at High-A last year, but he was only 19 years, and now he's still age appropriate at 20, and he's ripping it up with 8 homers and a 152 wRC+ in 24 games. The 24.8/7.9 K%/BB% still shows the rawness in his game, but his value is back on the rise with a nice looking lefty swing that is made for launch

Name: Yoelin Cespedes
Report: Cespedes was an explosion candidate in 2025, and while that didn't happen with a rough season, it's happening in 2026 with 7 homers and a 151 wRC+ in 26 games. He's definitely starting to fill out and he has a howitzer of a righty swing. The power is legit. The hit tool has turned into a risk though with a 30.4% whiff%, so he hasn't completely regained his past shine

Name: Malachi Witherspoon
Report: Malachi looks better than his highly drafted brother, Kyson, right now with a 2.66 xFIP (4.35 ERA) and a 32.6/6.7 K%/BB% in 20.2 IP at Single-A. Granted it's at a lower level, but Malachi is a big dude with big stuff and bat missing secondaries. The control looks good right now. Encouraging start to his career

Name: Kellon Lindsey
Report: Got a late start to the season but he's back on the rehab trail in rookie ball now

Name: JD Dix
Report: 71 wRC+ in 23 games at Single-A, but the 2 homers, 7 steals, and 22.0/12.8 K%/BB% all look good. He's been unlucky

Name: Hayden Alvarez
Report: Hit tool is taking a step back with a .255 BA and 23.8% K%. The 3 homers are nice to see in 26 games, but it comes with a 54.4% GB%. As I said this off-season, I like the talent, but have zero faith in the Angels to develop it, so I can't bet too hard on it

Name: Dean Moss
Report: 12.9/13.9 K%/BB% with 2 homers and 5 steals in 22 games at stateside rookie. He's only hitting .235 and the 22.3% whiff% isn't as impressive as the K rate, so I'm not going to fly him up the rankings, but I think that is a strong start and that he's living up to his billing as a strong hit tool hype

Name: Jordan Yost
Report: He looked much stronger this spring already and while he hasn't done anything in 9 games at Single-A with high groundball rates, I want to give him some more time

Name: Brendan Summerhill
Report: Not even the hit tool was transferring to Single-A with a 23.5% K% and .188 BA in 11 games and then he hit the IL

Name: Nestor German
Report: He's missing bats at Triple-A and has been solid with a 4.01 xFIP and 30.1/13.2 K%/BB%, but he looks more like a back end arm with a 92.7 MPH fastball

Name: Jose Urbina
Report: Off to a rough start at High-A but we are still in small enough sample land where I'll give him a bigger sample

Name: Miguel Mendez
Report: He was pitching well at Double-A but hasn't pitched since April 23rd for reasons I am unsure of

Name: Noble Meyer
Report: Yet to debut with a shoulder strain

Name: Boston Bateman
Report: 4.03 xFIP (5.32 ERA) with a 28.6/9.2 K%/BB% in 22 IP at High-A. Not exactly killing it, but good enough to want to see a bigger sample

Name: Thayron Liranzo
Report: Got a late start to the season due to an oblique strain and hasn't done anything in 6 games at Double-A yet

Name: Carson Roccaforte
Report: As a 24 year old at Double-A with a 30.1% K%, 35% whiff%, and .243 BA, it's highly likely the hit tool is not going to be good enough to a full time MLB player, but man is his fantasy upside so fun with lift/pull (8 homers), plus speed (9 steals) and plus CF defense. I think the proximity/upside combo deserves a spot

Name: Dakota Jordan
Report: 34.5% K% with a 148 wRC+ in 27 games at High-A says it all. The hit tool will likely never be good enough, but if he does get there in his mid to late 20's, the upside will be high

Name: Tony Blanco Jr.
Report: He's hitting .195 with a 36% whiff%. The hit tool is highly likely not to be good enough but he's such a power hitting beast I'll still give him a decent ranking

Name: CJ Hughes
Report: Off to a dominant start at stateside rookie, slashing .455/.625/.909 with 1 homer, 3 steals, and a 31.3/31.3 K%/BB% in 4 games. He was a pure projection play for Milwaukee as one of the youngest and skinniest in the draft. And of course, we love betting on Milwaukee. The biggest red flag is the 50% whiff%, but I've seen a lot of these rookie ball whiff rates (not just this season), and I'm not sure they are accurate honestly. There is something fishy about them.

Name: Junior Sanchez
Report: Sanchez is a short righty (5'10"), which is a profile that always struggles to gain too much steam in the rankings world, and he only throws low to mid 90's, but he's dominating High-A with a 1.96 ERA and 42.9/7.1 K%/BB% in 18.1 IP. I'm not really targeting him, but his performance deserves some respect

Name: Brady Ebel
Report: He's not hitting well but the plate skills are strong, he's running, he's not hitting the ball on the ground too much and the BABIP is low. I want to give him more time. And he's only 18

Name: Darell Morel
Report: Projectable 6'4'' uber talent who is off to a good start in stateside rookie with a 14.3/35.7% K%/BB%. The 36.8% whiff% isn't as good as the K rate, but on the other hand, the GB% is way down so far. Just a high upside kid I want to keep on an eye on at the least

Name: Kyle Lodise
Report: It's a repeat of last year with a terrible BA despite really strong contact rates at High-A. He doesn't have big raw power and he's lifting a lot, so the low BA isn't a total aberration, but I want to give it more time to see if it stabilizes at a higher level

Name: Gabriel Rincones
Report: His season is just getting started coming off a knee issue. Rincones is a proximity power play with some impressive EV/hard hit numbers

Name: Anderson De Los Santos
Report: Anderson is a surface stat play with excellent performance at Double-A, slashing .284/.431/.568 with 5 homers, 2 steals, and a 21.6/19.6 K%/BB% in 26 games. He's not a tools guy and I don't want to bet on him being an MLB starter, but I'll put him on as a surface stats play

Name: Handelfry Encarnacion
Report: He's still 18 years old in full season ball and he's hitting bombs with 5 homers in 29 games. The 25.9% whiff% looks better than the .211 BA. He's definitely been unlucky. The lefty swing is electric. I like the start

Name: James Ellwanger
Report: Big dude with big stuff who was off to a great start in 3 games at Single-A before going down with an elbow strain. Maybe with the injury he doesn't deserve to crack this list, but he would have been higher than this without the injury

Name: Tim Piasentin
Report: First few games in stateside rookie were horrific and it's a bad sign they started him there to begin with but I'll wait for a bigger sample

Name: Miguel Hernandez
Report: Hasn't done much in 2 games in stateside rookie

Name: Ronny Munoz
Report: DSL season starting in early June
